newsitem.title: USA: Montgomery Ward seeks $200 mln in immediate funds.
newsitem.headline: Montgomery Ward seeks $200 mln in immediate funds.

text.p: Montgomery Ward & Co needs $200 million in immediate financing to keep its operations running, the retailer said in a filing Tuesday in U.S. bankruptcy court here.
"The debtors have virtually no cash on hand," said Spencer Heine, executive vice president of the retailer, which filed Monday for protection under Chapter 11 of the U.S. bankruptcy code.

The 408-store chain already has a commitment from General Electric Co's General Electric Capital Corp for $1 billion in debtor-in-possession financing to cover inventory it will need for the fall and holiday season. But Heine said in a court filing that the company needed an additional $200 million in interim financing to cover liabilities right away.

"Absent interim financing for their continuing business operations, the debtors may have to curtail substantially continuing operations, resulting in immediate and irreparable harm to the value of their businesses and estates," the company said in court documents.

Montgomery Ward & Co listed assets of $4.1 billion and liabilities of $3.6 billion in its Chapter 11 filing. It sought bankruptcy protection after negotiations with lenders on a financial package to rescue the company collapsed.
